unit.title: Draw and interpret sketches and simple drawings

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Which drawing shows the main switch, the distribution boards and the cables between them as single lines, without showing where they are in the building?
options: A reflected ceiling plan
A wiring diagram
A single-line diagram
An elevation drawing

questions.stem: What is a reflected ceiling plan?
options: The ceiling drawn as if seen in a mirror on the floor
A plan of the floor drawn upside down for the ceiling fixer
A photo of the ceiling taken with the lights switched on
A section through the roof showing the rafters

questions.stem: A motor starter control circuit has one stop button and one start button. How are they normally drawn?
options: Both as normally open contacts, in parallel
Both as normally closed contacts, in series
Stop normally open, start normally closed, in parallel
Stop normally closed, start normally open, in series

questions.stem: In a direct-on-line starter circuit, a normally open auxiliary contact of the contactor is drawn in parallel with the start button. What is it for?
options: To stop the motor straight away if it is overloaded
To hold the coil on after the start button is let go
To reverse the direction in which the motor turns
To light a pilot lamp when the motor stops

questions.stem: On a contactor, which terminals are usually the coil?
options: 13 and 14
A1 and A2
21 and 22
95 and 96

questions.stem: By the usual numbering, what kind of auxiliary contact is marked 21–22?
options: Normally open
Overload trip
Coil supply
Normally closed

questions.stem: On a schematic, in which state are contacts and switches drawn?
options: At rest, with no power and nothing pressed or operated
In the state they are in while the machine is running
In whichever state makes the diagram easiest to draw
Always closed, so that the current path is easy to see

questions.stem: On a large control schematic, coil K3 has the numbers 4.2 and 6.5 written under it. What do they most likely tell you?
options: The voltage and current ratings of the coil K3
The time delay of the coil, in seconds
Where K3's contacts appear (page and column)
The order in which all of the coils switch on

questions.stem: Why are the wires in a control panel given numbers that match the schematic?
options: So the panel can be wired with fewer colours
So the wires can be cut to the same length
So the panel builder can be paid by the wire
So each wire can be traced on the drawing

questions.stem: A breaker in a board is labelled "Spare", but you find its outgoing cable is connected to outlets. What should you do?
options: Use it for the new circuit, since it is labelled spare
Trace the cable, correct the chart and tell the client
Remove the label so that nobody is confused
Leave it, since the label is the client's job

questions.stem: On a layout plan, a socket outlet symbol has "WP" beside it. What does this most likely mean?
options: Weatherproof
Wall plate
Water pump
Wired in parallel

questions.stem: A drawing note says "All outlets at 300 mm AFF u.n.o.". What does "u.n.o." mean?
options: Use new outlets
Under normal operation
Unless noted otherwise
Up to nine outlets

questions.stem: A drawing shows a 20 A breaker, but the circuit schedule in the specification says 16 A. What is the best action?
options: Fit 20 A, because a drawing is always newer than a schedule
Fit 16 A, because the smaller one is always safer
Raise a query and get a written answer before fitting
Fit whichever breaker is in stock at the time

questions.stem: Why is an isometric sketch often used to show a conduit run with bends in several directions?
options: It shows the run in three dimensions in one picture
It is the only kind of drawing that can be to scale
It shows the inside of the conduit and the cables
It needs no measurements at all to be useful

questions.stem: You sketch an existing panel so that a replacement can be ordered. Which information matters most on the sketch?
options: The colour of the wall the panel is fixed to
Sizes, fixing centres, cable entries and ratings
The name of the person who first installed it
Shading to show light and shadow on the panel

questions.stem: You make a site sketch of a room to plan new wiring. Why should each item be measured from at least two fixed points?
options: So the sketch fills the page more neatly
So the sketch can be drawn without a pencil
So no notes need to be written on it at all
So each position can be found again exactly

questions.stem: A switch room 7.2 m long must fit on an A3 sheet with about 300 mm of drawing space for its length. Which scale is the best choice?
On a 1:100 plan, a cable route measures 128 mm. Allowing 10% extra for drops and terminations, how much cable is needed?
A client's drawing uses symbols that your team has not seen before. What should you do first?
options: Guess from the shape which item each symbol is
Read that drawing's own legend (key)
Redraw it in your own symbols without asking
Leave out the items you do not recognise

questions.stem: On a single-line diagram, a cable is labelled "3C+E 6 mm² 25 m". What does this tell you?
options: Three cables of 6 mm² each, run 25 m apart
A 25 mm² cable with three 6 mm² earths
A 3-core and earth 6 mm² cable, 25 m long
The cable carries 3 circuits of 6 A for 25 m

questions.stem: Revision C of a drawing arrives while your team is halfway through work on revision B. What should the team leader do first?
options: Finish the job to revision B and file C for later
Hand out revision C and let each person read it on their own
Ask the client to cancel revision C to save time
Find what changed, stop affected work and brief the team

questions.stem: Which document usually tells you the type of cable, the earthing arrangement and the quality of fittings, rather than where they go?
options: The layout drawing
The title block
The specification
The site diary

questions.stem: In a three-storey building, which drawing best shows how the main supply rises from the ground-floor board to the boards on each floor?
options: A riser (vertical) diagram
A floor plan of the ground floor
A wiring diagram of one outlet
A detail of a ceiling rose

questions.stem: A section drawing through a wall shows a cable trunking above a suspended ceiling. Why is a section useful here?
options: It shows the colours of all the cables
It shows heights and what sits behind the finishes
It shows the price of the trunking per metre
It shows where the switches are on every floor

questions.stem: On site, a room measures 300 mm shorter than the plan says. Several boxes are dimensioned from the far wall. What is the best action?
options: Measure from the far wall anyway, exactly as it is drawn
Report it, and agree a reference point before marking
Scale the positions off the drawing with a rule
Leave out the boxes that no longer fit

questions.stem: In a ladder diagram, what do the two vertical lines at each side stand for?
options: The control supply, such as line and neutral
The walls of the control panel enclosure
The earth conductor and the cable screen
The start and the end of the motor winding

questions.stem: In a ladder diagram, why is each coil drawn at the right-hand end of its rung, next to the return line?
options: So that the coil can be seen from further away
So that the rung uses less wire in the panel
So the coil gets a higher voltage than the contacts
So all switching is on the line side, before the coil

questions.stem: On a CAD drawing, why is the electrical layout put on its own layer?
options: So that it prints in a larger font size
So the file can be opened on a phone with no CAD program
So it can be shown or hidden apart from the plan
So the drawing does not need a title block

questions.stem: A layout plan shows a dashed line from one switch to three lights, and the line continues to a fourth light in the next room. What does this tell you?
options: The fourth light needs its own breaker
The dashed line is a cable that is not needed
One switch controls all four lights
The lights in the second room are emergency lights

questions.stem: After a fault visit, why should your report include a simple sketch of how you found the wiring?
options: So the report is longer and looks more professional
So the customer does not need to pay for the visit
So the drawing office can skip updating its drawings
So others can see the problem and what was changed

questions.stem: Two contractors on the same site use different symbols for the same item. What is the best way to avoid mistakes?
options: Let each contractor keep using their own symbols
Agree one legend and use it on all the drawings
Remove all symbols and use only written words
Use colours instead of symbols on all drawings

questions.stem: Why should key positions on a layout be dimensioned from a column centre line rather than from a partition wall?
options: Columns are fixed, but partitions may move
Partition walls are never shown on electrical drawings
Column centre lines are always exactly 1 m apart
Sizes from walls cannot be checked on site

questions.stem: A solar PV system is drawn as boxes for the panels, inverter, batteries and distribution board, joined by arrows. What kind of drawing is this?
options: A block diagram
A wiring diagram
A floor plan
A section

questions.stem: On a single-line diagram, a breaker is marked "2P 32 A". What does "2P" mean?
options: 2 phases
2 poles
2 pieces
2 points

questions.stem: Before work starts, how should a team leader check a new set of electrical drawings?
options: Glance at the first sheet and file the rest
Check only the drawings that look complicated
Check the register, revisions, legend and notes
Wait until a problem shows up on site, then look

questions.stem: A panel general arrangement drawing shows the door, with dimensions to each device. What is it mainly used for?
options: To show how each device is wired inside
To list the cables leaving the panel
To show where the panel sits in the building
To mark out and cut the door for the devices

questions.stem: Why does each cable on a cable schedule have its own reference, such as C12, which is also marked on both ends of the cable?
options: So the cable can be sold back to the supplier later
So the cables can be pulled in number order
So the cable's price can be checked on the invoice
So each cable can be found and matched to its record

questions.stem: A schematic shows the overload relay's trip contact in series with the contactor coil. What happens when the overload trips?
options: The motor speeds up to clear the overload
The start button is held in until reset
The contact opens, so the coil drops out
The coil gets a higher voltage to hold in

questions.stem: When you sketch a panel layout on site, what is the best way to show the sizes clearly?
options: Draw roughly in proportion and write every size on it
Draw it exactly to scale with no sizes written on
Write the sizes in a list with no drawing at all
Take a photo only, without any measurements

questions.stem: A drawing has letters along the top and numbers down the side. A note says "see junction box at C4". How do you use this?
options: C4 is the fourth sheet of drawing C
Find the square where column C meets row 4
C4 is the box's cable size in mm²
C4 is the box's height in centimetres

questions.stem: During installation, a cable route was changed to avoid a beam. What must happen to the drawing?
options: Nothing, as the route is hidden in the ceiling
Mark the change so the as-built drawing is right
Throw the drawing away, as it is now out of date
Keep the change quiet to avoid extra paperwork

questions.stem: A floor plan's north arrow points to the top of the sheet. A board is drawn on the left-hand wall. Which side of the building is that wall on?
options: North
South
East
West

questions.stem: Why should superseded (out-of-date) drawings be stamped or removed from the site office?
options: So the office has more space for new drawings
So the drawing register can be thrown away
So nobody works from the wrong revision by mistake
So the client cannot see how the design changed

questions.stem: A trainee in your team cannot follow a control schematic. Which is the best way to help?
options: Trace one circuit with them, step by step, on the drawing
Tell them to read the drawing again until they get it
Wire it yourself so they do not hold up the job
Give them a different job with no drawings at all

questions.stem: A light fitting on a plan is tagged "Type L2", and a schedule in the drawing set lists Type L2. What does the schedule tell you?
options: Which room the fitting is in
The fitting's make-up, lamp, wattage and mounting
The name of the client who chose the fitting
How many hours the fitting has been used

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. You may add a neat sketch to an essay answer. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: A panel 600 mm wide is drawn at a scale of 1:5. How wide is it on the drawing, in millimetres?
What do the letters GA stand for, as in a panel GA drawing?
What do the letters IP stand for, as in IP65 written beside a light fitting?
By the usual numbering, which two terminal numbers mark an overload relay's normally closed trip contact?
By the usual numbering, give the terminal numbers of the first normally open auxiliary contact on a contactor.
What is the name of the table on a drawing that lists each change with its letter, date and who approved it?
What one word names the person who checks a drawing and signs the title block after the person who drew it?
What do we call the reference squares on a drawing, labelled with letters along one edge and numbers along the other?
What do the letters PV stand for on a solar power drawing?
What word is used for one outgoing position in a distribution board that feeds one circuit?
What is the name of the sheet that lists each type of light fitting with its lamp, wattage and mounting?
A 3.6 m wall is drawn 72 mm long. What is the scale? Write it as a ratio.
What is the name for a small part of a drawing shown again at a larger scale to make it clear, such as "A" on sheet 3?
A circuit chart lists 12 single-pole ways and 4 two-pole ways. How many single-pole spaces do they use in total?
What name is given to a drawing marked up by hand on site, often in red, to show changes before the office redraws it?

essays.stem: For a motor starter panel, explain the difference between the schematic diagram, the wiring diagram and the panel general arrangement (GA) drawing. Say who uses each one and when.
essays.modelAnswer: The schematic diagram shows how the circuit works. Each device is drawn as symbols in a logical order, from the supply at the top or left, through the contacts, to the coils, with no attention to where the parts sit in the panel. The designer draws it, and the electrician uses it to understand the circuit and for fault finding. The wiring diagram shows the real connections: each terminal of each device, the wire numbers and where each wire goes, laid out roughly as the devices sit in the panel. The panel wirer uses it to wire the panel, and the tester uses it to check each connection. The GA drawing shows the panel's outside and inside layout to scale: the enclosure size, door cut-outs, device positions, trunking, rails and gland plate. It is used to order the enclosure, mark out and cut the door, and fix the devices, and by the site team to check the space needed.
markingPoints: Schematic: how the circuit works, in logical order
Schematic used for understanding and fault finding
Wiring diagram: real terminals, wire numbers, used for wiring and checking
GA: physical layout to scale, door and device positions
GA used for ordering, marking out, fixing and checking space

essays.stem: Describe the control circuit of a direct-on-line starter with one stop button, one start button, a holding contact, an overload contact and a contactor coil. Explain what happens when start is pressed and released, when stop is pressed, and when the overload trips.
essays.modelAnswer: From the control supply, current flows through the overload relay's normally closed contact, then the normally closed stop button, then the normally open start button, and on to the contactor coil (A1–A2) and back to the return line. A normally open auxiliary contact of the contactor is wired in parallel with the start button. When start is pressed, the coil is energised, the main contacts close and the motor runs. At the same moment the auxiliary contact closes. When start is released, current keeps flowing through the auxiliary contact, so the coil stays on: this is the holding or latching contact. When stop is pressed, its contact opens, the coil drops out, the main and auxiliary contacts open, and the motor stops. It will not restart until start is pressed again. If the motor is overloaded, the overload relay's contact opens, the coil drops out and the motor stops in the same way. It must be reset before the motor can be restarted.
markingPoints: Correct order: overload NC, stop NC, start NO, coil
Holding contact in parallel with start
Start pressed: coil on, motor runs, holding contact closes
Start released: coil held in; stop pressed: coil drops out, motor stops
Overload trips: coil drops out, reset needed before restart

essays.stem: Describe how you would survey a small shop's electrical supply and produce a single-line diagram of it. Say what information the diagram should show.
essays.modelAnswer: I plan the survey with the owner and agree when boards may be opened. Any board covers are removed only with the circuits isolated where needed, or by a competent person following the Centre's or company's rules, and I never work live. I start at the supply intake and follow the system outward: the main switch, any sub-main cables, and each distribution board. For each board I record the incoming breaker, every outgoing way, the breaker type and rating, the circuit it feeds and the cable size and type, using the labels and by tracing where needed. I measure or estimate cable lengths. I then draw the single-line diagram, showing the supply at the top, the main switch, cables as single lines with their size, type and length, each board, and every outgoing circuit with its breaker rating and description. It should also show the earthing arrangement, RCDs, a legend, a title block with the date and my name, and a revision letter. Finally I check it against the site.
markingPoints: Plans the survey and works safely (no live work)
Follows the system from intake to every board
Records breakers, ratings, circuits and cable sizes and lengths
Diagram shows supply, main switch, boards, cables and circuits with ratings
Earthing, RCDs, legend, title block; checked against site

essays.stem: The contractor gives you the drawings and specification for wiring a small clinic. Describe what you would look for to find clashes and missing information, and how you would get answers before the team starts.
essays.modelAnswer: I first check the drawing register so I know I have every sheet at its latest revision, and that the specification matches. I read the notes, legend and title blocks. Then I compare the electrical drawings with the building drawings: do outlets clash with doors, windows, cupboards or sinks, and do lights clash with beams, ducts or air-conditioning units on the ceiling plan? I check that every item on the layout appears on the board schedule, that breaker ratings and cable sizes agree between the drawings and the specification, and that heights are given for every item. I look for missing information, such as no detail for the medical equipment outlets or no position for the main board. I list every question in a written query, with the drawing number and grid reference, and send it to the designer through my supervisor. I keep a log of queries and answers and mark the answers on the drawings so the team works from the same information.
markingPoints: Checks register, revisions, notes and legend
Compares electrical and building drawings for clashes
Checks schedules, ratings and sizes agree with the specification
Identifies missing information
Raises written queries with references and logs answers

essays.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would make a dimensioned sketch of an existing room's electrical installation so that the office can prepare a quotation for rewiring it.
essays.modelAnswer: I bring squared paper on a clipboard, a pencil and eraser, a tape and a laser measure, and a camera. First I draw the room's outline roughly in proportion, as a plan, with doors and windows, and mark north or the street side. I add every existing switch, outlet, light, fan and the board, using a simple legend. Then I measure: the room's overall length and width, the position of each item from two fixed points such as corners, and the heights of items and of the ceiling. I write each size on the sketch with dimension lines so they cannot be confused. I note the type and rating of items, the cable and containment used, the board's make-up, and anything the customer wants added. I take photos of each wall and the board, and label them to match the sketch. Finally I check that the measurements add up to the overall sizes, and I add the address, date and my name.
markingPoints: Right equipment: paper, pencil, tape or laser, camera
Outline in proportion with doors, windows and items in a legend
Measures from fixed points, with heights, on dimension lines
Notes types, ratings, containment and customer's requests; photos
Checks sizes add up; adds address, date and name

essays.stem: Explain how a floor plan and a reflected ceiling plan are used together to install the lights, smoke detectors and ceiling fans in an office.
essays.modelAnswer: The floor plan shows the walls, doors and the positions of switches, outlets and often the circuits from a view looking down. The reflected ceiling plan shows the ceiling as if it were seen in a mirror laid on the floor, so it lines up exactly with the floor plan: something in the top-left corner of the room is in the top-left corner on both drawings. The ceiling plan shows the ceiling grid, light fittings, smoke detectors, fans, air-conditioning grilles and access panels, with their positions and sometimes the ceiling height. I use the floor plan to find which switch controls each light and where the cables run, and the ceiling plan to set out exactly where each fitting goes and check that it does not clash with grilles, beams or sprinklers. I use the same reference lines, such as column centres, on both. If the two drawings disagree, I raise a query before cutting the ceiling.
markingPoints: Floor plan: walls, doors, switches, outlets, circuits
Ceiling plan seen as in a mirror, so it lines up with the floor plan
Ceiling plan shows grid, fittings, detectors, fans, other services
Uses both together: switching and cable routes, exact positions and clashes
Same reference lines; queries any disagreement before cutting

essays.stem: Explain how drawings should be controlled on an electrical installation site, from receiving a new revision to handing over the as-built drawings.
essays.modelAnswer: When a new revision arrives, it is entered in the drawing register with its number, revision letter and date. The team leader reads the revision table and clouds to see what has changed and tells the team. The old copies are collected and stamped "superseded" or destroyed, so nobody works from them, and one copy may be kept in a marked file for the record. Only current drawings are kept on site, in a clean, dry place. When work is done differently from the drawing, for example a cable route moved to avoid a beam, the change is agreed with the supervisor and marked by hand on a site copy, often in red, with the date and initials. These red-line drawings are kept up to date during the job. At the end, they are given to the office, which produces the as-built drawings. These show the installation as it really is, and are handed to the customer with the test results for future maintenance.
markingPoints: New revisions logged in the register
Changes read and the team told
Old copies stamped superseded or removed
Site changes marked up (red-line) with date and initials
As-built drawings produced and handed to the customer

essays.stem: Sites in Jamaica may receive drawings prepared to North American practice or to European (IEC) practice. Explain how this can affect reading the drawings, and what a team leader should do.
essays.modelAnswer: The two practices can use different symbols for the same item, for example a resistor drawn as a zigzag or a rectangle, and different contact symbols on schematics. They can also use different names: a switch called two-way in one may be called three-way in the other. Sizes may be in feet and inches instead of millimetres, and cable sizes may be given in AWG instead of square millimetres. Voltages, notes and abbreviations may also differ. If a trainee reads a drawing with the wrong system in mind, they could fit the wrong switch, order the wrong cable size or misread a height. A team leader should check which practice each drawing uses, read the legend and notes carefully, and brief the team. Where units differ, conversions should be worked out once and checked, for example in a table. Anything unclear should be raised as a written query with the designer, and the agreed meaning written on the drawings.
markingPoints: Different symbols for the same item
Different names (two-way and three-way switches)
Different units: feet and inches, AWG and mm²
Risk of wrong parts or sizes
Team leader checks legend, briefs team, checks conversions and raises queries

essays.stem: On a 1:100 plan, the cable route from a board to a water heater measures 145 mm. The cable also rises 2.0 m from the board to the ceiling and drops 1.6 m to the heater's isolator. Allow 0.5 m at each end for terminating and 10% for waste. Work out the length to order, and explain each step.
essays.modelAnswer: First I change the plan length to a real length. At 1:100, 145 mm on paper is 145 × 100 = 14 500 mm, which is 14.5 m. A plan only shows the horizontal route, so I add the vertical runs: 2.0 m up from the board and 1.6 m down to the isolator, giving 14.5 + 2.0 + 1.6 = 18.1 m. Next I add 0.5 m at each end for making off and terminating: 18.1 + 1.0 = 19.1 m. Then I add 10% for waste and small changes in the route: 19.1 × 1.1 = 21.01 m. Cable is cut in whole metres, so I round up and order 22 m. I would not round down, because a cable that is too short cannot be joined in most runs. I would also check the route on site, because the real path may differ from the straight line on the plan.
markingPoints: 14.5 m from the scale worked correctly
Adds vertical runs: 18.1 m
Adds terminating allowance: 19.1 m
Adds 10%: about 21 m, rounded up to 22 m with the reason
Mentions checking the real route on site

essays.stem: A newly wired control panel must be checked against its schematic and wiring diagram before it is powered. Explain how you would organise this check with your team.
essays.modelAnswer: I make sure we have the current revision of the schematic and wiring diagram, and that the panel is isolated, locked off and proved dead with a tester checked before and after. I give one member a clean copy of the drawings and a highlighter. Another member checks the panel. Working wire by wire, the checker finds each wire number, confirms that it goes from the right terminal to the right terminal, and tugs it gently to prove it is tight. The person with the drawing highlights each wire once it is confirmed. Where a wire is hidden, we use a continuity tester to prove the connection. Any wire that is missing, wrong or not on the drawing is written on a fault list and not corrected until the whole check is done. At the end, every line on the drawing should be highlighted. We then correct faults, recheck those wires, record the check and sign it before any power-on test by a competent person.
markingPoints: Current drawings; panel isolated and proved dead
Roles: one reads the drawing, one checks the panel
Wire-by-wire check with highlighting and continuity tests
Faults listed, corrected and rechecked
Check recorded and signed before power-on by a competent person

practical1.title: Survey a training room and produce a layout, single-line diagram and board schedule
practical1.brief: The assessor names a training room at the Centre with a visible electrical installation and a training distribution board. As a group, plan the survey and share the work. Each member sketches and measures one part of the room (two walls each, or the ceiling), recording the position of every switch, outlet, light and fan from fixed points. The assessor opens the training board with all circuits isolated so the group can read the breaker ratings and cable sizes; nobody touches anything inside. Then, together, produce on A3: a scaled layout plan (1:50 or as agreed) with a legend and title block; a single-line diagram from the board to each circuit; and a board schedule. Each drawing is checked by a member who did not draw it, and the checker signs it. Draw by hand or on the Centre's CAD software.
materials: A3 paper, squared paper, pencils, scale rule, set squares, eraser (or computers with CAD software)
5 m tapes and a laser distance meter
Clipboards and cameras or phones for photos
Blank board schedule form and title block template
Access to the training board, opened by the assessor with circuits isolated
photos: The group's plan with each member's part of the room
The board's breakers and labels as opened by the assessor
The finished scaled layout plan with legend and title block
The checker's signed check of each drawing
checklist: Measured their part of the room accurately from fixed points
Made a clear, dimensioned sketch in proportion
Used the right symbols and a legend
Drew to the chosen scale accurately (checked with a scale rule)
Showed ratings, cable sizes and circuit names correctly on the single-line diagram or schedule
Checked another member's drawing against the site and signed it
Worked safely and did not touch anything inside the board
safety: Only the assessor opens the board, with circuits isolated; nobody touches anything inside it
Do not climb on furniture to measure; use a laser meter or a safe step with a helper
Keep tapes and bags off walkways
Do not look into the laser of the distance meter

practical2.title: Draw the schematic and wiring diagram of a training control panel, then issue a revision
practical2.brief: The assessor gives the group a pre-wired training control panel (for example a direct-on-line starter with stop, start, overload, contactor and pilot light), isolated and locked off. As a group, prove it dead with a two-pole tester checked on a proving unit before and after. Then trace every wire, using the wire numbers and a continuity tester where needed, and record it. Each member traces part of the panel. Together, draw the schematic diagram and the wiring diagram, with terminal numbers, wire numbers, a legend and a title block marked Revision A. The assessor then gives a change: add a second stop button at a remote position and a "running" pilot light. Show the change as Revision B: cloud the changes, fill in the revision table, and list the new wires and terminals. Each member explains one part of the circuit to the assessor using the drawing.
materials: Pre-wired training control panel (isolated, locked off and tagged)
Two-pole voltage indicator, proving unit and continuity tester
A3 paper, pencils, rulers, symbol template (or computers with CAD software)
Highlighters and a trace record sheet
photos: The panel locked off and the tester being proved before and after the test for dead
Members tracing wires with the continuity tester
The Revision B drawing with clouds and the revision table filled in
A member explaining the circuit to the assessor
checklist: Took part in proving the panel dead correctly
Traced their part of the panel accurately and recorded it
Drew symbols, contacts and coils correctly, in the at-rest state
Showed terminal and wire numbers that match the panel
Showed the change correctly as Revision B, with clouds and the revision table
Explained how part of the circuit works using the drawing
Left the panel as found, still locked off, and the area tidy
safety: The panel stays isolated, locked off and tagged throughout
Prove dead with a two-pole tester checked on a proving unit before and after
Do not disconnect or change any wire; trace only
Return the panel to the assessor as found
